questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to be a good parent to teenagers
Why men become fathers and how fatherhood has changed
Why fewer people are having children
How mothers and fathers share the housework and childcare
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about fathers and how being a father has changed over the years.

questions.q: How does Catherine tease Neil at the start?
options: She says his grey hair and wrinkles are just his age
She says he is a bad father
She says he looks too young to be a dad
She says he talks about his children far too much at work
questions.why: When Neil mentions his grey hair and wrinkles, Catherine says 'I thought that was just your age.'

questions.q: What is one reason men become fathers, according to Dr Anna Machin?
options: Their parents want grandchildren
They want someone to look after them when they are old
They have a house and a job, so a family is the next stage
Their friends all have children
questions.why: She says for some it's a stage in life: 'They've got the house, they've got the job'.

questions.q: What do some men admit, according to Dr Machin?
options: They are afraid of babies
They don't really get on well with their partners any more
They want many children
They aren't keen, but their partner wants a baby
questions.why: She says some admit they're not that keen, but their partner wants a baby, so they go along with it.

questions.q: Why do a reasonable number of men want to be fathers?
options: To be better fathers than their own fathers were
To copy what their fathers did
To earn more respect from their colleagues at work
To make their mothers happy
questions.why: She says they want to undo what their father did to them and be a better father than he was.

questions.q: How does Dr Machin describe a typical '1950s father'?
options: Kind and playful
Always at home looking after the children and helping with homework
Distant, strict and not involved in daily care
Busy with housework
questions.why: She says a 1950s father was distant, disciplinarian and not involved in their children's daily life.

questions.q: What has Dr Machin seen in the 10 years she has studied fathers?
options: Fathers spend less time with their children
Fathers are much more involved with their children
More fathers are absent from home
Fathers have become stricter
questions.why: She says there has been 'a massive evolution in how hands-on fathers are'.

questions.q: Why does Neil say 'it serves you right' to Catherine?
options: Because she guessed the quiz answer
Because she was late
Because she laughed at the grey hair in his beard earlier
Because she ate his biscuit, which had been on the floor
questions.why: Catherine admits she ate his biscuit, and Neil says it had been on the floor.
